title: COP31 ends in failure as countries split over fossil fuels, climate finance
gist: COP31 in Antalya, Turkey ended without a consensus cover decision for the first time since 2009, as the EU, Latin American and Pacific Island states rejected the proposed Antalya Pact for omitting fossil fuels while the Arab League backed it and pushed for carbon capture. Narrower decisions on just transition and adaptation passed, but the outcome is widely seen as a serious setback for multilateral climate action.

insights.claim: The COP31 UN climate talks in Antalya ended without consensus on a cover decision for the first time since 2009, after running two days past schedule.
insights.speaker: Inside Climate News
insights.so_what: Weakening multilateral climate commitments reduces policy tailwinds for decarbonization investment.
insights.locator: For the first time since 2009, the conference

insights.claim: International collaboration on climate has declined since the 2023 Dubai agreement on transitioning away from fossil fuels, amid increased conflict, rising oil and gas prices, and economic insecurity.
insights.speaker: Inside Climate News
insights.so_what: Energy-security concerns are overriding climate ambition, supporting fossil-fuel demand persistence.

insights.claim: COP31 still adopted narrower decisions, including a program to help workers and communities transition away from fossil fuels and a plan to assess progress on climate adaptation.
insights.speaker: Inside Climate News
insights.so_what: Incremental adaptation and transition programs continue even as headline consensus fails.
insights.locator: For the first time since 2009, the conference

insights.claim: A central COP31 aim was to set quantifiable but voluntary global electrification goals and increase developed-country funding for adaptation in developing nations, neither of which made it into an agreed cover text.
insights.speaker: Inside Climate News
insights.so_what: Lack of electrification targets removes a potential demand signal for grid and clean-tech investment.
insights.locator: Cover decisions at the annual conferences

insights.claim: UN Secretary-General António Guterres said he was deeply disappointed at the lack of consensus but insisted fossil fuels are driving the climate crisis.
insights.speaker: Inside Climate News
insights.so_what: UN leadership continues to push fossil phase-out despite failed talks.
insights.quote: We can’t put out the fire while pouring fuel on it.

themes.theme: Fossil fuels and carbon capture divide

insights.claim: The European Union, representing 28 member countries, formally rejected the proposed Antalya Pact because it did not mention fossil fuels.
insights.speaker: Inside Climate News
insights.so_what: EU will likely continue unilateral climate policy, sustaining its carbon-pricing and clean-energy regime.
insights.quote: We will not endorse a decision that does not even mention fossil fuels

insights.claim: The 22-member League of Arab States backed the Antalya Pact, with Saudi Arabia's negotiator arguing developed countries used up most of the carbon budget and now ask developing countries to give up the energy sources that fueled their growth.
insights.speaker: Inside Climate News
insights.so_what: Oil producers are successfully resisting fossil phase-out language in UN processes.

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia's negotiator called resistance to including carbon dioxide removal and carbon capture and storage unscientific, while conceding CCS is not being deployed fast enough to keep 1.5 degrees within reach.
insights.speaker: Inside Climate News
insights.so_what: Petrostates are positioning CCS as the alternative to phase-out, supporting CCS policy demand.

insights.claim: The Marshall Islands rejected the Antalya Pact as a betrayal that benefits fossil fuel interests and threatens its security.
insights.speaker: Inside Climate News
insights.so_what: Vulnerable states are refusing compromise texts, making future consensus harder.
insights.quote: We will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests.
insights.locator: But compromise for the sake of consensus

insights.claim: Brazil and Egypt, hosts of the 2025 and 2023 talks, also criticized the COP31 text, with Brazil saying the conference failed to sustain momentum from its own talks.
insights.speaker: Inside Climate News
insights.so_what: Broad opposition across blocs underlines the fragmentation of climate diplomacy.
insights.locator: Egypt and Brazil, hosts of the UN
